research_question: Do different sample preservation methods (chilling only vs. acidification and chilling) significantly affect the measured concentrations of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in groundwater?

phase_1.user_prompt: I am evaluating the effect of adding hydrochloric acid (HCl) as a sample preservative for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in groundwater. I need to find the specific groundwater wells at the Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in southeastern Idaho that had paired unpreserved and preserved VOC samples collected in 2020 for quality assurance. Can you identify the USGS site numbers for these 26 wells and the 5-digit parameter codes for the 11 VOC analytes that were detected at or above their minimum reporting level in this study: cis-1,2-Dichloroethene, trans-1,2-Dichloroethene, 1,1-Dichloroethane, Chloroethane, Tetrachloroethene, Tetrachloromethane (carbon tetrachloride), Trichloroethene, Trichloromethane (chloroform), 1,1,1-Trichloroethane, Vinyl chloride, and 1,2-Dichloropropane?

phase_2.user_prompt: Now that we have the 26 site numbers and 11 VOC parameter codes, please download all the discrete water quality sample records for these wells for the year 2020. We need the raw concentrations, collection dates and times, and any metadata that distinguishes between preserved (acidified) and unpreserved samples; the two members of each pair are collected sequentially (a few minutes apart) on the same day at the same well.

phase_3.user_prompt: Process the water quality data to identify paired unpreserved and preserved samples collected sequentially at the same well. For each VOC analyte, retain only the sample-pairs where the reported concentration is at or above the minimum reporting level (MRL) in BOTH the unpreserved and preserved samples (the MRL is 0.1 or 0.2 ug/L depending on the analyte; see USGS National Water Quality Laboratory minimum reporting levels). Count the total number of valid analyte-pair detections that meet these criteria across all sites and analytes.

phase_4.user_prompt: Using the filtered paired-sample dataset of VOC concentrations above the MRL, perform a simple linear regression with the unpreserved sample concentrations as the predictor variable and the preserved sample concentrations as the response variable. What is the R-squared value of this regression? Additionally, summarize what this tells us about the comparability of the two preservation methods, and create a scatter plot of unpreserved vs. preserved concentrations saved as `voc_preservation_regression.png`.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The analysis demonstrates that the unpreserved and preserved sample results are highly correlated and statistically equivalent. Adding hydrochloric acid alongside chilling does not significantly alter the laboratory-determined concentrations of the evaluated VOCs compared to chilling alone.
checkpoint.visual_description: A scatter plot showing a strong positive linear relationship between unpreserved VOC concentrations (x-axis) and preserved VOC concentrations (y-axis). The points should tightly follow a 1:1 line or the regression line, indicating near-perfect correlation.
